subject: ophthalmology
title: Optic nerve disorders

steps.tx: **Papilloedema** swells both discs from raised intracranial pressure (tumours, hydrocephalus, venous sinus thrombosis, idiopathic intracranial hypertension in young obese women) with engorged veins, haemorrhages, preserved acuity early and enlarged blind spots; chronic disease pales into optic atrophy. Workup images brain with venography then measures opening pressure by lumbar puncture after mass exclusion; acetazolamide with weight loss treats IIH while shunting or fenestration rescues fulminant vision loss. Foster Kennedy (ipsilateral atrophy with contralateral oedema) localises frontal tumours.
steps.say: Swollen both discs with headaches and whooshing: scan brain, tap pressure after. IIH favours young obese women.

vis.alt: Fundus photograph showing severe bilateral optic disc swelling, blurred margins, engorged veins, and peripapillary hemorrhages, characteristic of acute papilloedema.
vis.caption: Acute papilloedema with disc swelling, engorged veins, and peripapillary haemorrhages

steps.tx: **Optic neuritis** (multiple sclerosis associated, typically young women) pains on eye movement with subacute unilateral vision loss, dyschromatopsia, afferent pupil defect and normal or mildly swollen disc (retrobulbar mostly); MRI brain with orbits shows demyelination while steroids hasten recovery without changing final acuity (optic neuritis treatment trial patterns). **Neuromyelitis optica** (aquaporin 4, bilateral severe with longitudinal myelitis) and MOG disease relapse aggressively needing plasma exchange and rituximab patterns. Children postviral cases recover better.
steps.say: Painful eye movements plus washed out colours in young woman: optic neuritis, MRI brain. Bilateral severe with spinal cord: NMO.

steps.tx: **Anterior ischaemic optic neuropathy**: nonarteritic (elderly vasculopaths waking with altitudinal field cut, crowded small discs, no pain) versus **arteritic** (giant cell arteritis with scalp tenderness, jaw claudication, raised ESR and CRP, chalky pallor) demanding immediate high dose steroids to save the fellow eye before temporal biopsy. Aspirin and risk control follow nonarteritic events while phosphodiesterase precipitants counselled. Posterior ischaemic variants complicate spine surgery hypotension bilaterally.
steps.say: Elderly waking half blind painlessly is nonarteritic; scalp tender with jaw pain is arteritic: steroids now.

steps.tx: Hereditary and compressive patterns: **Leber hereditary optic neuropathy** (young men, mitochondrial, painless bilateral sequential central scotomas with circumpapillary telangiectasia) counsels maternal inheritance with idebenone debates and smoking avoidance; dominant optic atrophy (OPA1, insidious temporal pallor) screens families. Compressive lesions (pituitary adenoma bitemporal hemianopia, meningioma, aneurysm) progress slowly with optic pallor and field cuts respecting vertical meridian; MRI with endocrine review precedes surgery. Toxic (ethambutol, methanol with putaminal necrosis) and nutritional (B12) neuropathies withdraw cause with replacement.
steps.say: Sequential central blind spots in young man: Leber mitochondrial. Bitemporal field cut: pituitary compression.
